identity.title: Conjunctival rim pallor (and palmar crease / nail-bed pallor)

technique.how: In good light, gently evert the lower eyelid and compare the colour of the anterior rim of the palpebral conjunctiva with the deeper posterior fornix: pallor is present when the anterior rim is as pale as the posterior conjunctiva (no red-pink contrast); absent when the rim is clearly redder. Also inspect palmar creases with fingers hyperextended and the nail beds.
technique.prerequisites: Daylight or bright white light; avoid comparison in jaundiced, very dark-skinned or conjunctivitis-affected eyes without allowing for it.

interpretation.positive_finding: Definite conjunctival pallor raises the probability of severe anaemia (Hb ≤9 g/dL) about four-fold (LR+ 4.4-4.5) and justifies an immediate haemoglobin; with tachycardia or hypotension consider occult haemorrhage.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of conjunctival pallor lowers the probability of severe anaemia only modestly (LR- 0.4-0.6) and does not exclude it; it is useless for mild-moderate anaemia.
interpretation.pitfalls: Interobserver agreement ranges from very poor (kappa 0.07) to good (0.75) depending on whether explicit criteria are used; palmar-crease and nail-bed pallor are not useful. Vasoconstriction (cold, shock) and poor lighting cause false positives.
interpretation.changes_what: Present: check haemoglobin now and look for a bleeding source if unstable. Absent: still send a haemoglobin when the presentation (dyspnoea, syncope, chest pain) makes anaemia plausible.

estimates.target_condition: Severe anemia, hemoglobin ≤90 g/L; finding = conjunctival pallor present (vs absent; borderline reported separately)
estimates.population: 302 medical and surgical inpatients, tertiary university-affiliated teaching hospital (Toronto); observers blinded to hemoglobin
estimates.quote: pallor present, LR 4.49 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.80, 10.99); … pallor absent, LR 0.61 (95% CI 0.44, 0.80)

estimates.target_condition: Severe anaemia, haemoglobin <9 g/dL; finding = severe (grade 3) conjunctival pallor for LR+, no conjunctival pallor (grade 0) for LR-
estimates.population: 390 consecutive patients >12 y from medicine outpatient and inpatient departments of a rural teaching hospital, India, 2007
estimates.reference_standard: Haemoglobin by electronic cell counter within one day of the pallor assessment
estimates.location: Table 2 (Likelihood ratios for pallor grades in diagnosing anaemia); columns are Hb <7, <9, <12 g/dL; values taken from the <9 g/dL column

sources.citation: Sheth TN, Choudhry NK, Bowes M, Detsky AS. The relation of conjunctival pallor to the presence of anemia. J Gen Intern Med. 1997.
Kalantri A, Karambelkar M, Joshi R, Kalantri S, Jajoo U. Accuracy and reliability of pallor for detecting anaemia: a hospital-based diagnostic accuracy study. PLoS One. 2010.
Nardone DA, Roth KM, Mazur DJ, McAfee JH. Usefulness of physical examination in detecting the presence or absence of anemia. Arch Intern Med. 1990.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use absent pallor to exclude anaemia or acute haemorrhage; do not grade pallor in poor light or in shocked, vasoconstricted patients.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Pallor with tachycardia, hypotension, melaena or haematemesis: treat as haemorrhagic shock (large-bore access, crossmatch) rather than waiting for the haemoglobin.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: With explicit rim-vs-fornix criteria, paired-observer kappa was 0.75 and 0.54 (Sheth 1997, Abstract); without them, kappa for conjunctival pallor was 0.07 (95% CI 0.04-0.14) (Kalantri 2010, Table 3) and 0.16-0.51 across sites (Nardone 1990, Abstract).

extraction_notes: Sheth 1997: severe anaemia prevalence not stated in the abstract; the 'borderline' category (LR 1.80, 95% CI 1.18-2.62, Abstract) was omitted from the estimate because the schema holds one LR pair. Kalantri 2010 Table 2 (PMC full text) gives conjunctival LRs at three thresholds; entered the <9 g/dL column (matching Sheth's ≤90 g/L). At <7 g/dL severe conjunctival pallor LR was 3.51 (0.76-16.1) and the 'no pallor' LR is printed as '–' (no severely anaemic patient lacked conjunctival pallor); at <12 g/dL severe pallor LR 4.25 (0.53-33.6), no pallor LR 0.40 (0.28-0.58) (Table 2). Moderate (grade 2) conjunctival pallor LR at <9 g/dL was 1.89 (1.45-2.46) (Table 2). Kalantri prevalence 0.21 = proportion with Hb <9 g/dL (Abstract). Nardone 1990 gives no conjunctiva-only sens/spec in the abstract; composites only: "pallor at any one of three sites (ie, the conjunctivae, face, or palms; 0.65)" sensitivity and "conjunctivae, face, and palms (all three in combination; 0.95)" specificity (Abstract, Results), so no Nardone estimate was entered; Nardone also concludes nail beds and palmar creases are not useful (Abstract).
